evidence.excerpt: When new items enter a catalogue they have no interaction history, and pure collaborative filtering fails. We use knowledge graph (KG) embeddings—specifically TransE and RotatE trained on a product attribute graph—to initialise item latent vectors before any interactions are observed. The KG is constructed from product metadata (category hierarchy, brand relations, material attributes) for a fashion retail domain, containing 41,000 entities and 210,000 triples. These embeddings are injected into a standard matrix factorisation model as a regularisation prior on the item factor matrix. On a cold-start evaluation protocol where test items have zero training interactions, our method achieves Recall@20 of 0.073 versus 0.031 for a content-based baseline and near-zero for pure CF. For warm items the KG prior adds a small but consistent improvement of 1–2% on NDCG@10. We provide ablations over embedding dimensionality and the weighting of the KG regularisation term.
